storage.intro: A pool combines disks into one storage space protected by RAID. Below: every disk and its health (SMART).
storage.unavailable: Disks cannot be read on this system. Storage Manager needs Linux with lsblk and smartctl.

smart.failedHelp: This disk reports that it is about to fail. Back up the data on it now, then replace the disk.
smart.warningHelp: This disk shows early signs of failure, such as bad or reallocated sectors. Data is still readable: back it up now and plan to replace the disk.
smart.standbyHelp: The disk is in power-saving mode. SMART is not read so the disk is not woken up; try again later.
smart.unsupportedHelp: This disk does not provide health data (common for virtual disks and some USB adapters).
smart.failingNote: Attributes marked red have crossed the manufacturer's threshold.
smart.warningNote: Attributes marked yellow have a non-zero value on a monitored damage counter.

usage.holder: Held by another device (device-mapper, multipath, or similar)
usage.zfs_label: Has a label from an inactive ZFS pool (deleted, or from another NAS)
usage.usb: Connected over USB: not used for pools unless allowed.
usage.identity: Same serial number or WWN as another disk (cheap USB enclosure), so the disk can’t be identified for sure.

https.title: The panel uses a secure connection
https.intro: The Sapo panel only opens over HTTPS so your password and data are encrypted on the network.
https.step1: Click the button below. Your browser will show a certificate warning because this certificate was created by the NAS itself, not by a certificate authority.
https.step2: Open the certificate details in that warning and make sure its SHA-256 fingerprint matches the one shown on the NAS screen (console login screen).
https.step3: If it matches, proceed to the site. This warning appears only once for this browser.
https.fingerprint: Certificate fingerprint (SHA-256). For convenience only: this page is not encrypted yet, so the trusted value is the one shown on the NAS screen.
https.why: If the fingerprint in your browser differs from the one on the NAS screen, do not proceed: another device may be impersonating your NAS. From now on, open the panel directly with its https:// address.

recovery.fileHint: Each code works only once. Keep them apart from your phone.
recovery.mustConfirm: Save the backup codes first, then tick this box.
recovery.needTwofa: Complete the two-step verification step first.

account.codesLow: Only {n} backup codes left. Create new ones so you can still sign in if you lose your phone.
account.codesNone: No backup codes yet. Create them now so you can still sign in if you lose your phone.
account.codesIntro: One-time codes to sign in when your authenticator app is not available.
account.codesWarn: All old codes stop working once new codes are created.
account.codesShownOnce: These codes are shown only once. Download or copy them now.
account.totpIntro: Move 2FA to a new phone or app, for example after signing in with a backup code because your old phone was lost.
account.totpScan: Scan this QR code with the new authenticator app, then enter its 6-digit code.
account.totpQr: QR code for the authenticator app
account.totpOldStillWorks: The old app keeps working until the code from the new app is confirmed.
account.totpDone: The new authenticator app is active. The old app no longer works.
account.othersSignedOut: Other devices signed in with this account have been signed out.
account.totpCodesStillValid: Your existing backup codes still work; create new ones if you suspect someone else knows them.
account.totpIntroOff: Protect your account with a code from an authenticator app on your phone, besides the password.

pool.title: Storage pools
pool.created: Pool {name} has been created and is ready to use.
pool.unavailable: Pools can’t be read on this system.
pool.zfsMissing: ZFS isn’t ready on this NAS, so pools can’t be created yet. Install the ZFS storage feature, then restart the NAS.
pool.none: No pools yet. Create a pool to start storing data.
pool.noneNoDisks: No pools yet, and no disk is available. Add a disk to create a pool.

health.degradedHelp: A disk has failed or is missing. Your data is still intact, but protection is reduced: replace the failing disk as soon as possible.
health.faultedHelp: The pool can’t be used. Don’t erase or format any disk; check the disk connections and the ZFS message below.

pool.almostFull: The pool is almost full. Above 80% ZFS slows down; delete data or add capacity.

scan.never: Never scrubbed. A scrub reads all data and repairs damage from healthy copies.

single.name: Single disk (no RAID)
single.desc: All capacity is usable, but if the disk fails all data is lost.

mirror.name: Mirror (RAID 1)
mirror.desc: Every disk holds the same copy. Simplest, and quickest to rebuild.

raidz1.name: RAID-Z1 (like RAID 5)
raidz1.desc: One disk’s worth of capacity is used for parity.

raidz2.name: RAID-Z2 (like RAID 6)
raidz2.desc: Two disks’ worth of capacity for parity. Recommended for large disks.

raidz3.name: RAID-Z3
raidz3.desc: Three disks’ worth of capacity for parity, for pools with many disks.

pool.tolerates: no disk can fail | 1 disk can fail | {n} disks can fail
pool.mixedSizes: The disks differ in size. Each disk is only used up to the smallest one ({size}).
pool.eraseWarning: All data on these disks will be permanently erased:
pool.pickLayout: Choose a layout that fits the number of disks.
pool.replaced: The disk is being replaced. ZFS is rebuilding data onto the new disk (resilver); the pool stays usable meanwhile.

shares.intro: Shared folders on a pool, opened from Windows, Mac, Linux, or phones over SMB, and from Linux or Mac over NFS.
shares.noPool: Create a pool first in Storage Manager.
shares.notShared: Nobody has access yet, so this folder can’t be opened from other computers.
shares.openFrom: Open from another computer (sign in with your panel username and password):
shares.deleteHelp: The folder {name} and ALL its contents ({used}) will be permanently deleted. This cannot be undone.
shares.aclPending: Applying permissions to the folder contents. This can take a while for large folders; until it finishes, new users may not open some files.
shares.aclError: Permissions couldn’t be applied to all folder contents: {message}
shares.syncPending: User or permission changes aren’t applied to the system yet; Sapo keeps retrying. Meanwhile folders are closed if accounts can’t be verified.
shares.nfsNoAccess: NFS isn’t active: {user} has no permission on this folder or the account is disabled. Grant access first, or pick another user.
shares.nfsHelp: NFS is used by Linux and Mac computers. NFS doesn’t ask for a password, so access is limited by computer address, and everything done from that computer counts as one Sapo user: it has exactly that user’s permissions on this folder.
shares.nfsClientsHelp: One per line: an IP address (192.168.1.20) or a network (192.168.1.0/24). Anyone at those addresses can open the folder without a password.
shares.nfsMount: Mount from Linux or Mac (NFS version 4):

network.intro: The NAS host name, the IP address of each network port (automatic from the router via DHCP, or a fixed address), and DNS.
network.unmanaged: Network settings haven’t been set from the panel (or were reset from the console recovery menu): every port uses DHCP.
network.hostnameHelp: Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. The panel is also reachable at https://{name}.local.
network.dnsHelp: One per line, up to three. Usually the router’s address.
network.warning: After applying, the new settings must be confirmed from the panel within a few minutes. If the panel can’t be opened at the new address, the old settings come back automatically. If you’re still locked out, use the recovery menu on the NAS console (reset network).
network.confirming: New settings applied. Waiting for confirmation, {seconds} seconds left before they’re reverted…
network.confirmHelp: The panel confirms by itself if it can still be reached at this address. If the NAS address changed, open one of the new addresses below to confirm (the browser will warn about the certificate again).
network.cancelled: Cancelled; the old settings were restored.
network.reverted: The new settings weren’t confirmed, so the old settings were restored.
network.pendingElsewhere: A network change is waiting for confirmation. If it isn’t confirmed, it will be reverted automatically.

confirmPage.ok: The new network settings were confirmed and saved.
confirmPage.failed: No network change is waiting for confirmation (it may already be confirmed, cancelled, or expired).

monitor.intro: System usage over the last 10 minutes, updated every {seconds} seconds while this window is open.

controlPanel.servicesHelp: Turning a service off disconnects every computer using it. Folder permissions don’t change; you can turn the service back on at any time.
controlPanel.smbHelp: Opens shared folders from File Explorer, Finder, or file apps.
controlPanel.nfsHelp: NFS exports set per folder in Shared Folders.
controlPanel.ntp: Set the clock automatically from the internet (NTP)
controlPanel.confirmOff: Turn off {name}? Every computer using folders through this service will be disconnected.
controlPanel.updatesHelp: Updates Debian and Sapo packages from the official repositories. Packages are never removed, and settings changed by the admin are kept.
controlPanel.upToDate: The system is up to date.
controlPanel.sapoUpdate: Sapo itself is being updated: the panel stops briefly and reconnects on its own.
controlPanel.installing: Installing updates… You can close this window; installation keeps running.
controlPanel.installFailed: The last update installation failed (code {code}). See the log.
controlPanel.installInterrupted: The last update installation stopped before finishing. Install again: the interrupted installation is resumed first.
controlPanel.webdavHelp: Opens Sapo Drive and shared folders at https://…/dav/ with an app password.

appCenter.intro: Additional apps from the Sapo catalog. Each app runs separately with its own account, without special privileges, and keeps its data on the pool you choose. Apps can only open the shared folders you give them.
appCenter.installHelp: The app image is downloaded the first time it starts (may take a few minutes). Memory limit {memory} MB.
appCenter.removeHelp: {name} is stopped and removed. Its data is kept, so you can install it again at any time.
appCenter.removeDataHelp: The app’s data ({id}) will be deleted permanently and can’t be recovered.
appCenter.foldersHelp: Choose the shared folders {name} may open. They appear at {path}/<folder name> inside the app. A running app is restarted so the change takes effect.
appCenter.foldersReadOnly: This app only gets read access.
appCenter.foldersNoShares: There are no shared folders yet. Create one in Shared Folders first.
appCenter.foldersExposure: Anyone who can open this app (from the network, including other apps on the NAS) can see these folders, subject to the app’s own login settings. Set up the app’s admin account right after installing it.

drive.intro: A personal folder for every user: only you can open it, from File Station or from other computers over the network.
drive.off: Sapo Drive isn’t turned on yet. Ask an administrator to turn it on.
drive.offAdmin: Sapo Drive isn’t turned on yet. Once it is, every user gets a personal folder on the pool you choose.
drive.enabled: Sapo Drive is on. Each user’s personal folder is being prepared.
drive.disabled: Sapo Drive is off. Personal folders are kept and come back when it’s turned on again on the same pool.
drive.smbHelp: From other computers on the network (sign in with your Sapo account):
drive.smbOff: Network access (SMB) is turned off by an administrator. You can still open the folder in File Station.
drive.defaultQuota: Default size limit per user (GB, empty = no limit)
drive.turnOffHelp: Personal folders can no longer be opened, but their contents are kept. Turning it on again on the same pool opens them again.
drive.userQuotaHelp: Empty = default limit, 0 = no limit. If the folder is already larger, existing files stay but no new files can be added.
drive.orphansHelp: Personal folders of deleted users (or on another pool). Their contents are kept until you delete them. A new user can’t take a name that still has a leftover folder.
drive.deleteHomeHelp: {user}’s personal folder and everything in it will be deleted permanently and can’t be recovered.
drive.webdavHelp: All folders you may open (My drive and shared folders) are at this address:
drive.webdavLogin: Sign in with username {user} and an app password (not your account password).
drive.webdavOff: WebDAV is turned off by an administrator.
drive.webdavCert: The NAS creates its own HTTPS certificate. To connect securely, download the certificate and mark it as trusted on that device. Don't turn off certificate checks: your app password could be stolen.

windows.title: Windows
windows.steps:
1. Install the NAS certificate: open sapo-nas.crt → Install Certificate → Local Machine → Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
2. File Explorer → right-click This PC → Map network drive.
3. Folder: {url}
4. Tick "Connect using different credentials", then sign in as {user} with the app password.

macos.title: macOS
macos.steps:
1. Open sapo-nas.crt (Keychain Access) and set the certificate to Always Trust.
2. Finder → Go → Connect to Server (⌘K), enter {url}.
3. Sign in as {user} with the app password.

ios.title: iPhone and iPad
ios.steps: Use a file manager app that supports WebDAV. Add a WebDAV server with address {url}, username {user}, and the app password. Install the NAS certificate via Settings → General → VPN & Device Management, then enable it in Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings.

android.title: Android
android.steps: Use a file manager app that supports WebDAV. Add a WebDAV server with address {url}, username {user}, and the app password. Install the NAS certificate via Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate.

rclone.title: rclone (two-way sync)
rclone.steps:
rclone config create sapo webdav url={url} vendor=other user={user} pass=$(rclone obscure 'APP-PASSWORD')

First sync:
rclone bisync ~/SapoDrive sapo:{'@'}home --resync --ca-cert sapo-nas.crt

Afterwards (for example on a schedule):
rclone bisync ~/SapoDrive sapo:{'@'}home --ca-cert sapo-nas.crt

drive.snapshotsHelp: One schedule for all personal folders. Snapshots don’t count toward users’ size limits.

appPasswords.title: App passwords (WebDAV)
appPasswords.help: For opening Sapo Drive and shared folders over WebDAV from a computer or phone, because WebDAV apps can't ask for a 2FA code. Create one per device; it only works for WebDAV, not for signing in to the panel. All app passwords are revoked when your account password changes.
appPasswords.onlyOnce: Copy it now: it won't be shown again. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.

snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.help: A snapshot keeps the state of a folder at a point in time, so deleted or changed files can be brought back. Snapshots only use space for what changed. In Windows, older versions appear under Properties → Previous Versions.
snapshots.summary: Keep {hourly} hourly, {daily} daily, {weekly} weekly (Monday); daily and weekly at {hour}:00
snapshots.offKeeps: Existing snapshots aren’t deleted when the schedule is turned off.
snapshots.deleteHelp: The old versions in this snapshot are lost for good.
snapshots.pruneConfirm: This new schedule will discard old snapshots beyond the number kept. Enter your password to continue.

external.title: External storage
external.help: Plugged-in USB drives. exFAT, FAT32, or NTFS drives can be mounted as an external folder for one group (read-only or read-write), opened from File Station, WebDAV, and SMB. Sapo never formats or changes a drive’s contents by itself. Eject a drive here before unplugging it.
external.none: No USB drives are plugged in.
external.name: Folder name
external.unmounted: {name} ejected; the drive can be unplugged.

reason.unsupported_fs: This format isn’t supported yet (only exFAT, FAT32, NTFS). Open Linux formats such as ext4 on a Linux computer.
reason.member: Member of a ZFS pool, RAID, LVM, encrypted, or swap: not mounted here.
reason.no_uuid: A file system without a UUID can’t be recognized when plugged in again.
reason.duplicate_uuid: Another drive has the same UUID (a clone): unplug one of them first.
reason.system_partition: System partition (EFI, Microsoft Reserved, or Recovery): not mounted here.

install.title: Sapo is running from RAM
install.help: All changes are lost when the NAS is turned off. Install Sapo to a system disk so the NAS boots from it; accounts, settings, and pools from this session are carried over.
install.running: Installing ({step})… Don’t turn off the NAS.
install.done: Sapo is installed on {disk}. Remove the ISO media (or change the boot order), then restart the NAS.
install.failed: Installation failed at step {step}: {error}. Data in pools wasn’t touched; fix the problem and try again.

backup.help: Backup copies a shared folder to another pool (for example a pool on a USB drive) every day. The first backup copies everything, later ones only what changed. The original folder is never changed.
backup.created: Backup task created. The first backup runs at the scheduled hour, or press Back up now.
backup.needTwoPools: Backup needs at least two pools. Create a second pool in Storage Manager, for example on a USB drive (turn on allow USB disks).
backup.started: Backup of {name} started in the background.
backup.keepWarning: The {n} oldest copies will be removed at the next backup.
backup.restoreHelp: The copy is restored as a new shared folder on the original pool, with the same permissions as the original folder. Existing folders are never overwritten.
backup.restoreStarted: Restore to folder {name} started. The folder appears in Shared Folders when done.
backup.deleteHelp: Deleting the task doesn't change the original folder. Copies on the destination pool are kept unless you choose to delete them.
backup.deleteData: Also delete all copies on pool {pool}
